newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ will publish new MCI index in June statement.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ will publish new MCI index in June statement.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Friday it would publish a new-style monetary conditions index (MCI) when it releases its Monetary Policy Statement next Friday.
It will publish both a nominal and real MCI.
The nominal index is a composite of 90-day bank bills and the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index.
It has been given an arbitrary base of 1000 based on the December 1996 quarter average rates of bank bills at 8.9 percent and the TWI at 67.1.
The index has been scaled so that a 100 point movement in the MCI is equivalent to a 100 basis point move in 90-day bank bills or a two percent change in the TWI.
This is consistent with the 2:1 ratio between the 90-day bank bills and the TWI as explained by the bank in its December statement.
The bank's desired conditions outlined in its March statement, of 7.5 percent for bank bills and 68.0 for the TWI, give an MCI of 925.
Using Friday morning's levels, of interest rates at 6.9 percent and the TWI at 67.5 ,the index was approximately 826.
